Thought: I need to determine which methods can be used to check the molecular weight of a purified protein. Let me analyze each option:

A. Analytical SEC (Size Exclusion Chromatography) - This technique separates proteins based on their size/molecular weight as they pass through a column filled with porous beads. Larger molecules elute faster than smaller ones, and by comparing with standards of known molecular weights, we can estimate the molecular weight of our protein. So this is a valid method.

B. Mass spectrometry - This technique directly measures the mass-to-charge ratio of ions, allowing for very precise determination of molecular weights. It's commonly used for protein molecular weight determination and provides high accuracy. So this is definitely a valid method.

C. SDS-PAGE (Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate-Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis) - This technique separates proteins based on their molecular weight as they migrate through a gel under an electric field. The SDS denatures proteins and gives them a uniform negative charge, so separation is based primarily on size/molecular weight. By comparing with standard markers, we can estimate the molecular weight of our protein. So this is also a valid method.

All three methods (Analytical SEC, Mass spectrometry, and SDS-PAGE) can be used to check the molecular weight of a purified protein, though they differ in their accuracy, resolution, and other characteristics.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A, B, C[/ANSWER]
